alt: A 400 kg boat with an engine force of 1500 N forwards, water resistance of 900 N and a wind force of 200 N backwards. The resultant force is 400 N forwards, so a = 400 ÷ 400 = 1.0 m/s².
caption: Add forces in the positive direction, subtract the others, then use F = m × a.

alt: A bar split into thinking distance, travelled at constant speed during the reaction time, and braking distance, travelled while the brakes act. Factors: speed and reaction time affect thinking distance; speed, mass, road conditions and worn tyres or brakes affect braking distance. At 0.70 s, 20 m/s gives 14 m and 40 m/s gives 28 m.
caption: Mass and road conditions affect braking distance only; reaction time affects thinking distance only.

alt: A velocity-time graph for a skydiver: velocity rises and levels off at terminal velocity, then drops when the parachute opens and levels at a lower terminal velocity. Force diagrams: air resistance less than weight while accelerating, equal at terminal velocity, greater just after the parachute opens, and equal again.
caption: Air resistance grows with speed until it equals weight; a parachute makes it bigger, so the skydiver slows to a lower terminal velocity.

alt: A spring hangs from a clamp beside a metre rule with a pointer and 100 g masses. A force-extension graph: the spring gives a straight line through the origin up to the limit of proportionality, then curves; a rubber band gives a curve.
caption: Extension is proportional to force in the initial straight region: Hooke's law.

alt: Two trolleys of 2.0 kg and 3.0 kg at rest with a spring between them. After release the 3.0 kg trolley moves right at 0.40 m/s. Momentum before is zero, so 1.2 + 2.0v = 0 and the 2.0 kg trolley moves left at 0.60 m/s.
caption: Total momentum stays zero: the lighter trolley moves off faster the other way.

alt: Force against time for stopping a 70 kg passenger moving at 15 m/s. Over 0.50 s with a seat belt and airbag the force is 2100 N; over about 0.05 s against a dashboard it is ten times larger. The momentum change, 1050 kg m/s, is the same.
caption: The same change in momentum over a longer time needs a smaller force.

alt: A light 2.0 m beam on supports A and B with a 600 N load 0.50 m from A. Taking moments about A gives R_B × 2.0 = 600 × 0.50, so R_B = 150 N, and R_A = 600 − 150 = 450 N.
caption: Take moments about one support, then balance the upward and downward forces.
